messages:
ops-bot: INCIDENT created: latency-surge / p95/p99 spike detected for continuous-batching (auto-paged eng-oncall). Alert ID: INC-2026-1764321000. Affected region: us-west-2. Symptoms: streaming stalls, elevated tail latency, increased retry counts.

mike-oncall: acked. grabbing metrics now.

mike-oncall: quick numbers from the dashboards — p95 jumped from 120ms -> 450ms, p99 ~ 2.3s on cont-batch path for streaming endpoints. streaming error-rate +3.2% in last 5m.

tara-sre: on it. do we have a recent rollout? any model changes or runtime flags?

ali-dev: no recent model changes, last deploy was 12h ago to a small canary. Runtime config unchanged. We saw some KV eviction warnings earlier but thought low impact.

mike-oncall: logs show batcher queue build-up on pool gpu-pool-7. looks like a small number of very long seq requests are delaying streaming batches. sample from batcher logs: 
```
[1764321001] pool=gpu-pool-7 batch_id=8421 size=64 duration_ms=1450 seq_max=4096 seq_median=128
[1764321002] pool=gpu-pool-7 batch_id=8422 size=60 duration_ms=1700 seq_max=8192 seq_median=96
```
These per-batch durations are pushing other streams into p99.

tara-sre: that matches mixed-seqlen amplification — a few huge sequences block the scheduler. We also have fairness scoring skewed; large requests not being preempted quickly.

ali-dev: checking scheduler metrics. batch_size_distribution shows heavy tail: many batches with 1-4 large sequences combined with many small ones. Continuous batching is not separating by seq length.

mike-oncall: customer impact — top customers with streaming usage: AcmeAI and BrightDesk. Both saw 5xx-retries and UX lag. CS jane-cs, can you confirm?

jane-cs: confirmed — AcmeAI reported timeouts from their side around 15:40ish. They said intermittent partial responses for long chats. escalating to AM.

tara-sre: mitigation options (quick):
- enforce max_batch_size cap for streaming on gpu-pool-7 to 32
- enable seq_length_preemption flag (runtime) to let long requests be moved to dedicated eviction queue
- apply batcher scheduling fairness bump (increase preemptiveness weight for streaming)
- temporarily route high-latency customers to us-east-1 fallback pool

mike-oncall: let's prioritize minimal blast radius: 1) set max_batch_size=32 on pool gpu-pool-7 (hot patch), 2) enable seq_length_preemption=true, 3) monitor for 10m, then decide on routing fallback.

ali-dev: prepping hotpatch. command: 
```bash
# patch batcher config via infra API
POST /infra/pools/gpu-pool-7/config 
{ "max_batch_size": 32, "seq_length_preemption": true }
```
Applying now to a single AZ sub-pool to be safer.

ops-bot: deploy-started: patch/gpu-pool-7-1764321105 by ali-dev. CI checks passed.

mike-oncall: rolling out to subpool-a. watching metrics.

(2m later)

ali-dev: patch applied to subpool-a. observing: average batch duration down ~30%, p95 reduced to ~220ms in that subpool.

tara-sre: good. push to subpool-b with 1% rollout, then full.

ops-bot: deploy-success: patch/gpu-pool-7-1764321128 to subpool-a.

(5m later)

mike-oncall: system-wide p95 now 180ms, p99 trending down from 2.3s -> 900ms. streaming stalls dropping. error-rate back to +0.8% above baseline.

jane-cs: AcmeAI confirms partial recovery, their timeouts dropped, but one customer session still saw a 5s stall. they want a postmortem.

tara-sre: next steps:
- finish rollout to all subpools (in progress),
- add a short-term routing rule: any request with declared seq_len > 2048 -> route to dedicated long-seq queue (no continuous batching)
- schedule a follow-up to tune batching thresholds and fairness algorithm (owners: tara + ali)

ali-dev: rolling to subpool-b now. ops-bot: starting rollout.

ops-bot: deploy-started: patch/gpu-pool-7-1764321180 to subpool-b by ali-dev.

(3m later)

ops-bot: deploy-success: patch/gpu-pool-7-1764321205 to subpool-b.

mike-oncall: full pool patched. metrics look stable. p95 ~160ms, p99 ~420ms. still higher than baseline but within SLO throttle window.

tara-sre: for the postmortem: collect sample batches that had seq_max>4096, scheduler traces, and the fairness scoring logs for last 6h. also add a regression check to detect future regressions when mixed sequence traffic increases.

ali-dev: noted. I'll dump batch traces: 
```bash
GET /infra/metrics?query=batcher_scheduling_trace&from=1764318000&to=1764322000 | jq . > /tmp/batch-traces.json
```

mike-oncall: customer impact summary for incident ticket: AcmeAI had ~47 requests affected with tail latencies >3s, BrightDesk saw ~18 requests. overall <0.05% of streaming traffic. No data leakage, only availability/latency impact. Severity: Sev3.

jane-cs: filing customer-facing note and offering a timeline + runbook actions. will coordinate with PM.

ops-bot: incident-transition: mitigation in place. monitoring for 30m. Assigned to tara-sre for follow-up investigation and ali-dev for batching algorithm changes.

mike-oncall: handing off to tara (overnight). I'll leave alerts unmuted, add notes on runbook. Oncall next: tara-sre please ack takeover.

tara-sre: ack takeover. will run the postmortem and schedule a follow-up deep-dive tomorrow. leaving a short checklist:
- collect traces + metrics (ali)
- run fairness simulation with current traffic profile (ali + tara)
- propose batching thresholds and long-seq routing rule (PR target EOD tomorrow)
- customer comms drafted (jane)

mike-oncall: thanks all. marking incident as mitigated in channel but keeping thread open for follow-ups. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: INCIDENT update: status=mitigated, INC-2026-1764321000.

tara-sre: closing handoff. I'll ping here with the postmortem link once ready.

mike-oncall: thanks — handing off timestamp 1764321365.
